I'm psyched for Fallout's third season whenever it comes out (Kyle MacLachlan says it could be May or June next year), but I'd be perfectly happy if it had an ending and the show was done. Better to tell your story and leave it there than drag out a show just because it's popular and end up finishing on a wet fart of a finale when you should have gone out on, er, whatever the opposite of a wet fart is. Season 3 has finished filming, but right now not even Walton Goggins, who plays The Ghoul, is sure what the future holds for Fallout's TV incarnation. Talking about how the show's maintaining the "subversive humor and the satirical kind of elements" it brought over from the games at an awards screening attended by GamesRadar, he said, "I feel confident that we've done that in season three, and if we get the opportunity to come back for season four, that would continue to honor how sacred this is to people. It's not something that we take lightly." Goggins as we know doesn't play videogames himself. And co-star Aaron Moten has sworn off playing Fallout, leaving Ella Purnell the only actor to roll a Vault Dweller out of the headline trio. But despite that, Goggins is still aware of what the games mean to people. "I mean, my son is a gamer. I see exactly how and why he plays games. I'm not a gamer at all, but the game of Fallout has been around for such a long time. It's been a shared experience between parents and their children and friends for such a long time, but it holds a very special place in their heart," Goggins said. "I think what they have responded to, at least what I've been told out on the road, is the reverence in which all of us approach the sacred nature of this game, and while still keeping it an original story in the canon of Fallout." The Ghoul is still on the hunt for his family in Fallout, with actor Walton Goggins saying the ongoing search could change his character's outlook in the third season of the Prime Video series. "If you never got to see a loved one, and you found out that those loved ones were still alive, what might you experience after not seeing them for a very long period of time, what would that mean to you?" Goggins pondered about the Ghoul's upcoming arc at an awards screening attended by GamesRadar+. As a refresher, the Fallout season 2 ending saw the Ghoul uncovering at least part of the mystery of his missing wife and daughter – namely, that they were still alive. But they were since taken to Colorado for reasons unknown, with the Ghoul on their tail. "So that's what we all spent the better part of this season really asking ourselves, and you know whether I discover them or whether I don't discover them in season three is really irrelevant to me," Goggins added. Then, a line that cuts deep into the Ghoul's motivations for the upcoming season: "Well, then, what does that mean to you if you get what you've been looking for for 200 years? And how does that change you? What does that really mean to you?" So, when might Fallout next drop on our screens? Recently, we had a bombshell courtesy of Hank actor Kyle MacLachlan, who told a fan that the third season could drop in May or June of next year. Beyond that, who knows? Goggins himself doesn't have the intel on a fourth season, and a recent Instagram post from the actor sounded more like a goodbye to the show than we were expecting.
